matches.candidate_construct: LIPT1 is required for transfer of lipoic acid to selected 2-ketoacid dehydrogenase proteins, allowing their lipoylation and activation
matches.canonical_construct: Citrin is the mitochondrial aspartate-glutamate carrier that exports aspartate to the cytosol while importing glutamate plus a proton
matches.canonical_vignette: A 27-year-old man has recurrent episodes of confusion after carbohydrate-rich meals. During an episode, plasma ammonia and citrulline are markedly elevated. He has a longstanding preference for protein- and fat-rich foods. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in SLC25A13.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which mitochondrial transport process is most directly impaired?

canonical_options.A: Import of ornithine from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
canonical_options.B: Export of aspartate from the mitochondrial matrix in exchange for glutamate plus a proton
canonical_options.C: Export of citrate from the mitochondrial matrix in exchange for malate
canonical_options.D: Import of pyruvate from the cytosol into the mitochondrial matrix
canonical_options.E: Exchange of cytosolic ADP for mitochondrial ATP across the inner mitochondrial membrane

matches.candidate_construct: PMPCA encodes the alpha subunit of mitochondrial processing peptidase, which is required for maturation of many imported nuclear-encoded mitochondrial precursor proteins
matches.canonical_construct: AGK is a kinase-independent subunit of the TIM22 complex required for import and assembly of mitochondrial carrier proteins
matches.canonical_vignette: A newborn has bilateral congenital cataracts, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and persistent lactic acidosis. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in AGK. Patient fibroblasts contain a destabilized inner-mitochondrial-membrane protein-import complex and reduced abundance of several mitochondrial carrier proteins.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which cellular function is most directly impaired?

canonical_options.A: Recognition of N-terminal mitochondrial targeting sequences by the TOM20 receptor
canonical_options.B: Cleavage of mitochondrial targeting peptides by the matrix processing peptidase
canonical_options.C: Import of presequence-containing proteins into the mitochondrial matrix through the TIM23 complex
canonical_options.D: TIM22-dependent import and assembly of multipass mitochondrial carrier proteins into the inner membrane
canonical_options.E: TAFAZZIN-dependent remodeling of cardiolipin acyl chains within the inner mitochondrial membrane

matches.candidate_construct: PGM3 converts N-acetylglucosamine-6-phosphate to N-acetylglucosamine-1-phosphate during UDP-GlcNAc synthesis
matches.canonical_construct: PMM2 encodes phosphomannomutase 2, which converts mannose-6-phosphate to mannose-1-phosphate. Loss of PMM2 lowers the mannose-1-phosphate/GDP-mannose pool and impairs synthesis of lipid-linked oligosaccharides required for N-linked protein glycosylation.
matches.canonical_vignette: An infant has hypotonia, developmental delay, esotropia, inverted nipples, abnormal suprapubic fat pads, and cerebellar hypoplasia. Serum transferrin glycoform analysis suggests a congenital disorder of N-linked glycosylation, and genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in PMM2.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which metabolic conversion is most directly impaired?

canonical_options.A: Mannose-6-phosphate tagging of lysosomal hydrolases in the Golgi apparatus
canonical_options.C: Fructose-1-phosphate to dihydroxyacetone phosphate and glyceraldehyde

matches.candidate_construct: LRPPRC forms an RNA-binding complex that stabilizes mitochondrial mRNAs and supports their polyadenylation and coordinated translation
matches.canonical_construct: ETHE1 is a mitochondrial sulfur dioxygenase; its loss causes sulfide accumulation that inhibits cytochrome c oxidase
matches.canonical_vignette: A 2-year-old boy has developmental regression, chronic diarrhea, recurrent petechiae and acrocyanosis, and episodic metabolic acidosis. Urine contains markedly increased ethylmalonic acid, and plasma C4 and C5 acylcarnitines are elevated. Muscle biopsy shows reduced cytochrome c oxidase activity. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in ETHE1.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which mechanism most directly explains the respiratory-chain abnormality?

canonical_options.A: Failure to insert copper into cytochrome c oxidase, preventing assembly of complex IV
canonical_options.B: Failure of mitochondrial sulfide oxidation, causing hydrogen sulfide accumulation that secondarily inhibits cytochrome c oxidase
canonical_options.C: Defective transfer of electrons from succinate to ubiquinone at respiratory-chain complex II
canonical_options.D: Failure to synthesize mitochondrial-encoded cytochrome c oxidase subunits because of mitochondrial DNA depletion
canonical_options.E: Failure of coenzyme Q biosynthesis, limiting electron transfer from complexes I and II to complex III

matches.candidate_construct: SLC30A10 is a cell-surface manganese efflux transporter; loss of trafficking or efflux function causes cellular and systemic manganese accumulation
matches.canonical_construct: ATP7B loss impairs biliary copper excretion and copper incorporation into ceruloplasmin, causing toxic copper accumulation in liver, brain, and cornea.
matches.canonical_vignette: A 19-year-old man has tremor, personality change, elevated aminotransferases, and Kayser-Fleischer rings. Genetic testing identifies biallelic ATP7B variants.
matches.canonical_lead_in: Which physiologic process is most directly impaired?

canonical_options.B: Hepatic excretion of copper into bile
